definition.simple: The process of putting seeds into the soil so they can grow into plants.
definition.academic: Sowing is the agricultural process of planting seeds in the soil at the correct depth and distance to ensure proper germination and crop yield.

examples: A farmer scattering wheat seeds across a prepared field.
Using a machine to place corn seeds exactly 2 inches deep in the ground.

common_misconceptions: Just throwing seeds anywhere on the ground is called sowing. (Truth: Proper sowing requires correct depth and spacing.)
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what would happen if seeds are planted too close together or too deep in the soil.
